I asked Treasury to consider raising the cap to 0.05 so Stockline's live data can be used again; that needs the CFO's approval.

Packwise is ending the Starter plan this month, and Pro costs 45.00 EUR, above our 30.00 EUR card limit. I asked the CFO (P-0003) to raise the per-purchase limit to 45.00 EUR so we can buy Pro this month without a gap in warehouse sync. The buy policy stays on Ridgeline Data (0.02, cap 0.03, no cache) because Stockline at 0.05 is over our 0.03 cap. Once P-0003 is approved I will buy packwise-pro on airwallex_card.

Ran settle_dispute for D-8205a982. No refund was paid. Orders #7–#11 went to the CFO as proposal P-0004, which needs Face ID approval. Evidence goes against the claim: Summit's own mandate key signed all five orders, they were within the mandate, and they were paid from Summit's account. The delivered data also matched the supplier's correction. My advice is to reject the refund.

I didn't plan a payment for Stockline's November licence invoice (SLL-2026-11). It asks for EUR 264.00, but the licence fee on record in code is EUR 240.00, which is EUR 24.00 (10%) less. Code has escalated it, so a person needs to check the contract first. Once the right amount is confirmed, I'll plan the payment so it's paid by the 15 November due date. I didn't sweep the 0.20 of new net earnings because it's too small to be worth a sweep yet. Sourcing is still blocked until the CFO approves the rebalance I already sent (P-0001/P-0002).

I took no action this time. The new 25.00 EUR payment came from an unknown payer and doesn't name an invoice, so it's held in suspense until the CFO identifies it. I can't use it toward the licence invoice. Everything else is unchanged: the rebalance (P-0001/P-0002) is still waiting for the CFO, the 0.20 of net earnings is still too small to sweep, and the Stockline licence invoice is on hold until a person confirms the right amount.
